basis: Angel/spirit of the early-medieval Latin Solomonic magic tradition (Ars Notoria, Liber Juratus, Liber Razielis)

entities.name: The Seven Planetary Angels of the Grimoire Tradition
entities.primary_domains: planetary governance; astral magic; the seven heavens; planetary hours
entities.source: Klaassen, The Transformations of Magic; Boudet, Entre science et nigromance
entities.note: The set of seven angels governing the planetary spheres standardized in medieval Latin astral-magic and Solomonic texts: Cassiel (Saturn), Sachiel (Jupiter), Samael (Mars), Michael (Sun), Anael (Venus), Raphael (Mercury), Gabriel (Moon).

entities.name: The Angels of the Ars Notoria
entities.primary_domains: infused knowledge; memory; eloquence; the liberal arts; theology; angelic mediation
entities.source: Ars Notoria (ed./trans. Veronese); Klaassen, The Transformations of Magic
entities.note: The angels invoked through the notae and orationes of the Ars Notoria so the operator might receive, through angelic mediation, instantaneous infused knowledge and perfect memory of the liberal arts, theology and Scripture.

entities.name: Cassiel
entities.primary_domains: Saturn; restriction; time; melancholy; the seventh sphere
entities.source: Liber Razielis; Boudet, Entre science et nigromance
entities.note: Cassiel (Cafziel/Captiel) is named in the Latin astral-magic tradition as the angel presiding over the sphere and hours of Saturn.

entities.name: Sachiel
entities.primary_domains: Jupiter; prosperity; benevolence; expansion; the sixth sphere
entities.source: Liber Razielis; Boudet, Entre science et nigromance
entities.note: Sachiel (Zachariel) is named in the Latin Solomonic corpus as the angel governing the sphere and hours of Jupiter, invoked for prosperity and favor.

entities.name: Anael (Angel of Venus)
entities.primary_domains: Venus; love; concord; beauty; the third sphere; astral magic
entities.source: Liber Razielis; Boudet, Entre science et nigromance
entities.note: Anael (Anachiel/Haniel) is named in the Latin astral-magic tradition as the angel of the sphere of Venus; shares its name with the Testament-of-Solomon Anael (ENT_LAT_ANAEL).

entities.name: Samael (Angel of Mars)
entities.primary_domains: Mars; war; severity; iron; the fifth sphere; martial hours
entities.source: Liber Razielis; Klaassen, The Transformations of Magic
entities.note: In the medieval Latin planetary-angel scheme Samael is assigned to the sphere of Mars; functionally distinct from the Gnostic/demiurgic Samael (ENT_GNO_SAMAEL) though sharing the name.

entities.name: The Angelic Kings of the Air (Liber Juratus)
entities.primary_domains: the four directions; the winds; days of the week; planetary rule; spirits of the air
entities.source: Liber Juratus Honorii (ed. Hedegard); Kieckhefer, Forbidden Rites
entities.note: The Sworn Book of Honorius names the kings of the air ruling the cardinal directions and the days/planets, each commanding subordinate aerial spirits, summoned within the operation aimed at the beatific vision.

entities.name: Operation of the Beatific Vision (Liber Juratus)
entities.primary_domains: vision of God; angelic ascent; purification; consecration; divine names
entities.source: Liber Juratus Honorii (ed. Hedegard); Klaassen, The Transformations of Magic
entities.note: The central operation of the Sworn Book is a regimen of purification, prayer and consecration culminating in the operator's attainment of the beatific vision (the direct sight of God) mediated by angels.

entities.name: The Notae of the Ars Notoria
entities.primary_domains: infused knowledge; memory; the liberal arts; visual contemplation; angelic transmission
entities.source: Ars Notoria (ed./trans. Veronese); Klaassen, The Transformations of Magic
entities.note: The notae are the complex diagrammatic figures, inscribed with names of angels and verba ignota, contemplated while reciting the orationes; presented as a heaven-sent art by which knowledge of the sciences is infused.

entities.name: The Semiforas / Schemhamphoras Names (Liber Razielis)
entities.primary_domains: divine names; the ineffable Name; power over creation; astral and angelic operations
entities.source: Liber Razielis (Latin, compiled for Alfonso X); Boudet, Entre science et nigromance
entities.note: The Latin Liber Razielis transmits the Semiforas (a Latinization of Shem ha-Mephorash, the 'explicit Name'), powerful divine names revealed to Adam and the patriarchs conferring authority over creation and the angels.

entities.name: Genon and the Angelic Teachers of Eloquence (Ars Notoria)
entities.primary_domains: eloquence; the trivium; grammar, rhetoric, dialectic; infused speech
entities.note: Among the angels named in the orationes and notae of the Ars Notoria are figures invoked specifically for eloquence and the arts of the trivium.

relationships.rationale: The seven planetary angels collectively govern the seven planetary spheres in the Latin astral-magic scheme.
The planetary angels are invoked in the elective astral-magic operations of the Latin Solomonic corpus.
Cassiel is the Saturn member of the grimoire seven-planetary-angel set.
Cassiel presides over the sphere of Saturn.
Sachiel is the Jupiter member of the grimoire seven-planetary-angel set.
Sachiel presides over the sphere of Jupiter.
Anael is the Venus member of the grimoire seven-planetary-angel set.
Anael governs the sphere and operations of Venus.
Homonym/continuity: the grimoire Venus-angel Anael shares its name and Venusian association with the Testament-of-Solomon Anael.
Samael is the Mars member of the grimoire seven-planetary-angel set.
Samael presides over the sphere of Mars.
Homonym: the Mars planetary-angel Samael shares its name with the Gnostic/demiurgic Samael, functionally distinct.
The canonical archangel Michael is the Sun member of the grimoire seven-planetary-angel set.
Michael governs the sphere and operations of the Sun in the grimoire planetary scheme.
The canonical archangel Raphael is the Mercury member of the grimoire seven-planetary-angel set.
Raphael governs the sphere of Mercury.
Raphael, the Mercury/healing angel, is invoked for healing operations in the grimoire tradition.
The canonical archangel Gabriel is the Moon member of the grimoire seven-planetary-angel set.
Gabriel governs the sphere and operations of the Moon in the grimoire planetary scheme.
The angels of the Ars Notoria mediate the infused knowledge that is the goal of the operation.
The Ars Notoria frames angelic transmission of knowledge as a divine revelation renewing Solomon's wisdom.
The Ars Notoria presents its angelic knowledge as the art God's angel taught Solomon, the legendary recipient.
The eloquence-teaching angels named in the orationes belong to the Ars Notoria angelic collective.
These angels confer infused mastery of the trivium and eloquence.
The notae are the figures, inscribed with angel names, contemplated to invoke the Ars Notoria angels.
Contemplation of the notae with the orationes is the means by which the sciences are infused.
The kings of the air are summoned within the magical operations of the Sworn Book of Honorius.
The Liber Juratus kings of the air are correlated with the days/planets and the cardinal directions.
The central operation of the Sworn Book aims at the beatific vision, a direct revelation of God.
The operation invokes and constrains the angelic kings of the air en route to the beatific vision.
The operation deploys divine names for the operator's protection while constraining the summoned spirits.
The Semiforas are presented as divine names revealed to Adam and the patriarchs.
The Latin Liber Razielis attributes its revealed names to the angel Raziel's book given to Adam.
The Semiforas names confer protection and authority over creation and spirits.
